blocks.html:
Contract implemented by a search engine provider. Optional methods
(`swapIndex` and `waitForTask`) are omitted from the abstract class on
purpose — define only those your engine can back. `searchMany` has a default
that runs `search` concurrently; override it to pack queries into one
engine round-trip.

types.name: identifier
types.description:
Each search provider has a unique identifier, such as `search-medusa`, used to
register it and to bind an index definition to it. An index definition
selects a provider by setting its `provider` property to this identifier. You can also use this identifier
in `medusa-config.ts` to configure the default provider for the Search Module.

On a provider extending `AbstractSearchProviderService`, this is derived from
the class's `static identifier` property.
types.example: class MySearchProviderService extends AbstractSearchProviderService { static identifier = "my-search" // ... }

blocks.html:
This method creates or updates the index at `index.physical_name` to match the definition.
The Search Module calls it for every definition when migrations run.

You may recreate the index if your engine can't alter a schema in place. That's safe:
the module only points this at an index it's about to seed, never at one that has to
keep serving reads, and never during a partial rebuild.

Throw if the definition asks for something your engine can't hold, such as a
facet type it doesn't support. Since migrations run before the application
serves requests, the error surfaces at startup rather than as wrong results
later.

types.name: input
types.description: The index to create or update.

children.name: index
children.description:

including the `physical_name` to create it under, the `primary_key` its

blocks.html:
This method points a logical index at a different physical index, which the
Search Module uses to reindex without downtime: it seeds a shadow index, then
swaps it in.

Implementing this method is optional. When it's not implemented, the module
reindexes in place instead, leaving the index incomplete while it's seeded.

blocks.html:
This method adds documents to an index, replacing any that already exist under the same
ID. The Search Module uses it both for direct writes and for seeding, where it's called
once per batch.

If your engine applies writes later rather than inline, return a task with an `id` and
implement `waitForTask`, so the module can wait before swapping a new index in.

Write to `input.index` but read schema information from `input.definition`:
during a swap, `input.index` is the shadow index being seeded, whereas the
definition is that of the logical index.

The index's physical name. This is the index to

children.name: definition
children.description:
The logical definition whose documents are being written. `index` can
point at a shadow physical index during a swap, so providers must use
this value for schema information and `index` for the destination.

blocks.html:
This method removes every document matching the given filters.

Deleting by ID isn't a special case — it arrives as a filter on the primary key, such
as `{ id: ["prod_1", "prod_2"] }`. Recognize that shape and use your engine's
delete-by-ID path, which is usually much faster. If your engine can't delete by
arbitrary filters, either search first and delete the matching IDs, or throw.

types.name: input
types.description:
The index and the filters
selecting the documents to remove.

children.name: index
children.description: The physical name of the index to delete the documents from.

children.name: filters
children.description:
The filters selecting the documents to remove. Deleting by ID is a filter on
the index's primary key, such as `{ id: ["prod_1", "prod_2"] }`.

children.name: $and
children.description: Filters that must all match.

children.name: $or
children.description: Filters of which at least one must match.

children.name: $not
children.description: Filters that must not match.

children.name: q
children.description:
The free-text query. Sits among the filters so a `query.graph` call converts
to `query.search` unchanged; the module lifts it out before compiling the
rest, so a provider never sees `q` as a field.

blocks.html:
This method runs a search against an index. The Search Module will use this method in
its `search` and `searchMany` methods.

The free-text query arrives as `q`, already lifted out of `filters` passed to `query.search` or
the Search Module's service. `attributes_to_retrieve` includes only the fields that the
search engine can serve.

Compile `input.filters` to your engine's filter syntax, and reject the
operators it can't express rather than approximating them. Also, use
`input.index.physical_name` as the index to query, not `input.index.name`,
since the two differ under an index prefix or during a swap.

types.name: input
types.description:
The query, the resolved index
definition, and the attributes to return.

children.name: index
children.description:
The resolved definition of the index to query. Use its `physical_name` as
the index to query, since it differs from the index's name under an index
prefix or while a swap builds a replacement.

children.name: name
children.description:
The index's unique name, which is what `query.search({ entity })` resolves
against.

children.description: The `query.graph` entrypoint used to hydrate non-indexed fields.

index or on reindex.

children.description: The settings applied to the index.

children.description:

drifted from its definition and must be migrated.

children.name: physical_name
children.description:
The concrete index the provider reads and writes. Differs from `name` under
an index prefix, or while a `swap` builds into a replacement.

children.name: attributes_to_retrieve
children.description:
The field paths the search engine must return on every hit. Already narrowed
by the Search Module to the fields the index can serve, so project it as
given.

children.name: q
children.description:
Lifted out of `filters` by the module, because `filters` compiles to a DSL
with no representation for free text.

children.name: filters
children.description: The filters to apply, including the free-text query as `q`.

children.name: $and
children.description: Filters that must all match.

children.name: $or
children.description: Filters of which at least one must match.

children.name: $not
children.description: Filters that must not match.

children.name: q
children.description:
The free-text query. Sits among the filters so a `query.graph` call converts
to `query.search` unchanged; the module lifts it out before compiling the
rest, so a provider never sees `q` as a field.

children.name: pagination
children.description: How the results are paginated and sorted.

children.name: skip
children.description:
The number of documents to skip before the returned hits. Mutually exclusive
with `cursor`.

children.name: take
children.description: The maximum number of hits to return.

children.name: order
children.description:
The fields to sort the hits by, keyed by the field's dotted path. The
reserved `_score` key sorts by relevance.

children.name: cursor
children.description:
An opaque provider cursor, as returned in a previous result's
`metadata.next_cursor`. Mutually exclusive with `skip`.

children.name: search_options
children.description: The options changing how the query is matched, scored, and aggregated.

children.name: attributes_to_search_on
children.description:
The dotted paths of the fields to match the free-text query against. Defaults
to every field marked `searchable` on the index.

children.name: match_strategy
children.description:
How query terms combine.

- `"all"` (default): every term must appear as a complete token.
- `"any"`: at least one term must match.
- `"last"`: typeahead. Completed terms must match in full; the last term
  is a prefix, so `"my sear"` matches `"My search results"`.

children.name: typo_tolerance
children.description: Whether to match terms that are misspelled by a character or two.

children.name: facets
children.description:
The facets to compute alongside the hits. A string is shorthand for a `value`
facet on that field.

children.name: disjunctive_facets
children.description:
Compute each facet ignoring the filter on that same field, so a storefront
keeps showing sibling values of an active filter. Needs one query per facet
on every engine reviewed, so the module expands them and hands the set to
`provider.searchMany`.

children.name: highlight
children.description: How the matched terms are highlighted in the returned hits.

children.name: distinct
children.description: Return at most one hit per distinct value of this field.

children.name: min_score
children.description: Discard hits scoring below this threshold.

children.name: include_score
children.description: Whether to return each hit's relevance score.

children.name: locales
children.description:
Query-time language hint, e.g. `["en"]`. Engines that analyze per language
(Meilisearch, Algolia) use it to pick the analyzer; a provider that cannot
honour it rejects it rather than silently matching differently. Defaults to
the index' `settings.locales`.

children.name: vector
children.description:
The options of a vector, or semantic, search to run instead of, or alongside,
the free-text query.

children.name: count
children.description:
How the total number of matching documents is computed. `"exact"` may be
rejected or slow depending on the provider.

children.name: provider_options
children.description:
Escape hatch for engine features the interface does not model, keyed by
provider identifier, e.g. `{ typesense: { drop_tokens_threshold: 0 } }`.

types.name: Promise
types.description: The hits, any facets, and the metadata.

blocks.html:
This method runs multiple queries in a single request to the search engine.
The Search Module uses it for its `searchMany` method, including the extra
queries produced by disjunctive faceting.

Implementing this method is optional. When it's not implemented, the module
runs the queries in parallel `search` calls instead. Override it to pack the
queries into one engine round-trip.

blocks.html:
This method waits until a deferred write is applied. The Search Module uses it
to wait for a seed to be applied before swapping the new index in.

Implement it if your engine acknowledges writes and applies them later. When
it's not implemented, the module assumes a write is applied once
`upsertDocuments` resolves.

types.name: task
types.description:
The task returned by the write, holding the `id`
that identifies it.

children.name: id
children.description:
The ID identifying the write in the search engine, which is passed back to
the provider's `waitForTask` method. It's set only for a deferred write,
since a provider applying writes inline has nothing to identify.

children.name: index
children.description: The name of the index the write was applied to.

children.name: status
children.description: The write's status.

children.name: error
children.description: The error that made the write fail, if its `status` is `failed`.

children.name: message
children.description: The error's message.

children.name: code
children.description: The error's code, as reported by the search engine.

children.name: timeout_ms
children.description:
How long to wait for the task before
giving up, in milliseconds.
